Acquisition appraisal for Related · Draft for discussion · October 2026

Roehampton Sports Ground Estate

Priory Lane and Bank Lane, London SW15 5JQ. Thirty-eight freehold acres owned by the Bank of England since 1908, home of the Wimbledon Qualifying Competition, offered as a whole or in four lots by Knight Frank. This brief sets out the estate, the income in place, BGP's commercial business plan and the working underwrite. The National Tennis Centre stays exactly as it is on the LTA's 125-year lease. The Grange residential conversion is left for Related to value.

The estate

Four lots, four different uses

Knight Frank invite offers for the whole, individual lots or combinations. The Bank reserves the right not to accept the highest offer, bids go in a prescribed format, and AML information is required at heads of terms. The site sits 500 m north of Richmond Park, with Barnes station 0.8 miles away.

The Grange costs money from January 2027.

Gerald Eve's service charge budget for the year to March 2026 is £695,823 (£7.84 per sq ft over an 88,739 sq ft apportionment that appears to include other occupiers). The landlord bears the void share, and empty rates follow. Budget around £1m a year to hold the building empty until Related's conversion starts.

The AELTG step-up depends on the break.

Rent doubles to £675,000 on 1 August 2031. The tenant can walk away on 31 July 2031. In the current lease the uplift is only worth what the All England Club decides it is worth in 2031, which is the opening for a renegotiation now.

The business plan

Three moves

Take a surrender of the All England Club's 2036 lease and regrant a 10-year lease of the grounds and the hospitality space they actually use for the Qualifying, let about 50,000 sq ft of the leisure buildings to Third Space on a 20-year lease, and hand The Grange to Related for a residential conversion. The cottages are sold or let with vacant possession. Lot 1 is not part of the plan: the National Tennis Centre remains the National Tennis Centre, the LTA keeps its lease to 2129 and no surrender or variation is proposed.

Move 1

Surrender and regrant with the All England Club

£100,000 pa

The Club surrenders its lease of the whole of Lot 2, which runs to 2036 with a 2031 break, and takes a new 10-year lease of the playing fields, the hospitality part of the Pavilion, the long-standing temporary pavilion and the marquee rights already consented to 2031. The sports hall, pool, squash courts and car parks come back to the landlord on the day of the surrender.

The Club's lease is outside the Act and runs to 2036, so the surrender has to be agreed, not imposed. Their lever is the 2031 break; ours is certainty of tenure for the Qualifying and a rent that falls from £350,000 to £100,000 for a smaller demise. Document the surrender and regrant as a condition of the purchase so the leisure buildings are vacant on completion.

Move 2

Let c. 50,000 sq ft to Third Space

£1.50m pa

Third Space need about 50,000 sq ft GIA, not the whole 68,153 sq ft. A 20-year lease at £30 per sq ft GIA with two years rent free and a capital contribution equal to one year's rent. Rent indexed to CPI, reviewed five-yearly, capped at 3 percent a year.

Splitting the leisure buildings

How 50,000 sq ft comes out of 68,153

Measured from the Principal Plans GIA drawings (September 2019). The Sports Club is the pool and sports hall building, 32,377 sq ft over four levels. The Pavilion is the 1920s clubhouse, 32,543 sq ft: an east block of changing rooms and offices, a central section of bars and kitchens, the main function hall running west, and a long column-free annex at the south-west end that reads as the long-standing temporary pavilion. The squash courts are a separate 3,233 sq ft building. The Club needs the hospitality space for the Qualifying; Third Space need the pool, hall and studios.

What the Club needs in Qualifying week.

Player and official facilities, hospitality, media and storage for a two-week event. Under Option B+ they keep the function hall, first-floor lounge, roof terrace and the annex, 18,602 sq ft, plus the temporary pavilion and the marquee and grandstand consents; under Option B they also keep the central bars, 22,313 sq ft in all. The sports hall and pool are not event space and sit better with the gym year-round.

How the areas were measured.

The green GIA outlines were extracted from the Principal Plans PDFs and reproduce the schedule to within 0.1 sq m on every sheet. The split lines were then cut through those outlines: Option B's line follows the wall between the east block and the central bars, Option B+ moves it one section west. Principal Plans should confirm from the CAD before pricing, but these are measured figures, not estimates. The underwrite below uses 50,000 sq ft and can be changed.

Parking

Can the estate give Third Space 150 spaces and The Grange 30?

Yes on the marked bays that already exist. We traced every marked bay on the Warner Surveys topographic survey of August 2019, registering its ten sheets to the Ordnance Survey grid, and found 198 marked bays in two car parks, against a requirement of 180. The constraint is policy and ownership, not space: new hardstanding on Metropolitan Open Land will be resisted, and the main car park has to be in the right lot and outside the Club's new demise.

Residents from Bank Lane, Third Space from the north-east

Access 1, Bank Lane, residential. The gated, tree-lined drive on the survey leads to the Grange forecourt and the two southern blocks of car park A. Residents never cross the gym traffic. Access 2, the estate road from the north-east, Third Space. Runs past the sports hall exit to car park B and on round the Sports Club to the main blocks of car park A, which is where the Sports Club entrance faces. A barrier across the drive just beyond the two southern blocks keeps the two apart: the residents' side holds 37 bays, and the 23 bays lining the rest of the drive are reached from the car park's internal road on the Third Space side, not from Bank Lane. Gates and barriers of that kind are permitted development. Both accesses exist, so using them this way is not development; the only test they face is the highways question in the Grange's Class MA prior approval, which now concerns 30 residential spaces on Bank Lane only. Check two things on title: the right of way over Priory Lane that benefits title 239100, and that the 2004 Tennis Centre lease reserves the landlord's rights over any part of the estate road inside the LTA demise.

Car park A and the Club's new lease.

Buying the whole estate makes this simple: car park A is yours whichever lot the brochure puts it in. The brochure lot plan draws The Grange's parking as the land running from the building to Bank Lane, and the surveyed drive also runs to Bank Lane, so A is very likely the Grange car park and today sits inside the Club's demise. It comes back on the surrender; the new lease must exclude both car parks, and the Grange's 30 spaces and Third Space's 150 are then allocated by the landlord.

Policy.

Wandsworth is Inner London for London Plan standards. Priory Lane is low PTAL, where the residential maximum is around 0.5 spaces per home at PTAL 0 to 1 and 0.25 at PTAL 2 to 3. Thirty spaces for 50 to 70 homes is 0.4 to 0.6 per home, at or above the cap depending on PTAL. Under Class MA the spaces are existing and highways impact, not a parking ratio, is the test. Third Space's 150 is a tenant requirement, met from existing tarmac without any change of use of open land.

Underwrite

Commercial underwrite, three-year hold

Every figure in the left-hand panel is a BGP working assumption and can be changed. The model buys the whole estate in January 2027, sells the cottages, does the landlord's works in 2027, starts the Third Space lease in January 2028, takes the Club's surrender and regrants from 2028, and sells the commercial lots at the end of the hold on net initial yields with purchaser's costs deducted. The Grange is treated as sold to Related; leave Related's number blank and the model shows the price Related would need to pay for the bid to clear the target profit on cost. Debt is drawn against costs as they fall, interest is paid from income or equity, and the loan is repaid from sale proceeds.

Planning and risk

Buying without planning risk

The test for every part of the plan is that it works on existing consents, existing use classes and existing hardstanding, with nothing that needs a planning permission to make the numbers work. The table shows where each element stands. The one element that still needs a consent is The Grange conversion. Class MA prior approval is a 56-day, limited-test process, not a planning application, and the Bank is submitting it; the answer is sequencing, with the prior approval in hand before exchange or exchange conditional on it.

ElementPlanning positionStatusHow to keep it risk-free

Internal works are not development. The spa, sauna, creche and pool alterations were consented in 2007 and 2011 and are built.ExistingKeep the works inside the existing envelope. The Bank obtains the prior approval before exchange, or exchange is conditional on it. The approval runs with the building and transfers on purchase; the conversion must then complete within three years.
The Grange: Class MA summary

What the residential permitted development route needs

The brochure says a detailed planning summary and the technical documents for the PD application are in the Knight Frank data room. They were not in the files we received, and the Wandsworth planning history runs only to the March 2026 lawful development certificate for the grounds building, so the application has not been registered. Ask Knight Frank for the PD pack. Against the Class MA tests as they stand after the March 2024 changes:

  • Class E use for two years before the application. Offices since at least 2017, when the ground floor South Wing changed from leisure to office. Met.
  • Vacancy. The three-month vacancy test was removed in 2024. The ITF leases end 31 December 2026 in any case.
  • Floorspace cap. The 1,500 sq m limit was removed in 2024, so the whole 5,361 sq m can convert.
  • Exclusions. Not listed, not in a Conservation Area, not a scheduled monument or safety hazard area. Metropolitan Open Land is not an exclusion from Class MA.
  • Prior approval matters. Transport and highways, contamination, flooding, noise from commercial neighbours, natural light to every habitable room, fire safety where the building is 18 m or more, and adequate space standards. The transport test is where the 30 existing spaces and the shared car park come in.
  • Grounds building and courts. Nothing in Class MA allows external works, so balconies, new openings or a roof extension would need a full application on MOL. Related's scheme should assume conversion within the envelope.
Risk register
High

The surrender itself. The Club's lease runs to 2036 outside the Act, so the surrender and regrant must be signed up before exchange, with the new lease excluding the leisure buildings and both car parks. Without it, Move 2 cannot start until 2031 or 2036.

High

Third Space covenant and terms. A 20-year lease on about 50,000 sq ft at £30 GIA with three years of incentives is the whole commercial value. Covenant strength, guarantor and the works specification need agreeing before the bid.

High

Grange prior approval. The conversion depends on Class MA prior approval, not yet applied for. Make it a condition of exchange or wait for the Bank's grant; the 56-day determination fits the timetable to a January 2027 completion.

Medium

Parking. 198 marked bays traced from the 2019 survey against 180 needed. Car park A sits inside the Club's demise today, so the new lease must exclude both car parks.

Medium

Holding cost of The Grange. Around £1m a year empty from January 2027 until Related take it.

Medium

Guarantor on the Tennis Centre lease. Due diligence only; the LTA lease is not being touched. The 2011 deed substituted LTA CLG Ltd for the All England Club. Confirm the brochure's "Lawn Tennis Association Limited" is the same entity, and that nothing has changed since.

Low

Title. Rent-charges of £57 from a 1779 deed on titles 239100 and 396768; Registrar's restrictions against charges on the older titles; a 1997 sub-station lease and 2009 EDF transformer lease; a right of way over part of Clarence House. Nothing seen that blocks the plan.

Low

VAT. Brochure says The Grange is opted to tax; Gerald Eve's 2025 budget says the landlord has not waived exemption. Reconcile before structuring.

Note

Environmental. Groundsure Siteguard (September 2019) concluded acceptable environmental risk for banking security; Part 2A or third-party action unlikely.

Planning history
  • Metropolitan Open Land across the whole estate. Not listed, not in a Conservation Area. The Wandsworth Local Plan 2023-2038 (partial review 2026) and the London Plan 2021 apply. Policy LP54 strongly resists loss of sports pitches, playing fields, indoor sports facilities and land last used for outdoor sport.
  • Wimbledon Qualifying consents: 2025/4672 approved January 2026 for marquees and temporary facilities for five years; 2024/0088 for marquees and grandstands; a 2023 amendment to add grandstands was refused and later consented properly. 2025/2066 approved a new grounds maintenance building; 2026/1109 a lawful development certificate for its construction compound.
  • Sports Centre: 2004/2604 new west entrance with canopy and ramps and veranda infill; 2004/5058 two floodlit hard courts; 2007/3262 sauna, steam room and spa extension and new west entrance and canopy to the sports hall and pool building; 2008/4309 medical clinic in the pool building; 2011/5340 creche extension to the clubhouse; 2011/3582 storage building.
  • The Grange: 2005/5242 access ramp; 2017/2937 ground floor South Wing from leisure to office.
  • National Tennis Centre consent 2003/2964, with an Environmental Statement, provided the replacement courts and pitches for the Bank's sports club; 2009/0937 seasonal canopy over two clay courts.
